- Can we co-term any uplift to our Jan 1 renewal so we’re not on staggered invoices? Also looking for a shortfall/grace credit for the first 30 days if our forecast overshoots.

Subject: Re: Planning for August cohort increase — short-term uplift options

Hi Emily — thanks for the context and the report. We can absolutely support a short-term uplift; below are three practical options with tradeoffs so you can pick what fits operationally: 

1) Temporary burst bucket (90 days): +30% committed uplift on your current committed units, billed monthly, with a 10% up-front discount on the uplift portion. No long-term commit, auto-reverts at end of 90 days.

2) Staged top-up (3-month prorated reserve): you commit to the uplift for 3 months at a higher discount (15%) if you agree to convert to a 6-month top-up within the first 60 days (co-term option at that point).

3) Short dedicated pool (ideal if latency-critical): reserved capacity for 90 days at list rates with a 60-day grace for overages (we'll credit overage above forecast up to one month).

For co-terming to Jan 1: we can pro-rata the uplift amount and create a one-line amendment that aligns the uplift with your Jan 1 renewal; invoicing would be pro-rata for the remaining year after Jan 1.

If you’d like, I can run exact pricing on the attached usage and send a redline-ready amendment + DocuSign link. Deadlines: if you want the burst in place before Aug 1, we’d need a signed amendment by July 20.

Short answer: yes on uplift; several ways to protect you for shortfalls. Tell me which option you prefer and I’ll put numbers on it.

— Priyom Das
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
